architecture.mechanism: cathodic polarization at -0.95 VCSE inhibits SRB biofilm formation and promotes protective calcareous deposit formation, improving corrosion resistance at coating defects
architecture.intervention: increase cathodic protection potential from -0.85 V to -0.95 V at the far ends of the pipeline using distributed, low-power auxiliary anodes (e.g., mixed metal oxide or graphite) placed along the pipeline without excavation, leveraging existing rectifier capacity via optimized current distribution
architecture.expected_effect: reduced current drain from coating holidays, stabilized pipe-to-soil potential at -0.95 V, inhibition of microbial activity at defect sites, and formation of protective calcareous deposits that passivate exposed steel and reduce localized corrosion
architecture.falsification_test: deploy temporary auxiliary anodes at 500m intervals along the pipeline, measure pipe-to-soil potential at defect sites after 14 days, and compare biofilm presence (via microbial swab testing) and calcareous deposit formation (via ultrasonic thickness testing) to baseline sections
